text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - The UK's leading blue-chip index finished little changed after an earlier Wall Street-inspired rally reversed and dragged British shares off their best levels, dealers said. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,762.4, up 3.9 points or 0.08 percent.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index surged to its seventh consecutive record closing high in bourse dealings, underpinned by the dollar rising to 1.76 marks in European dealings and higher German debt prices. The DAX-30 index closed at 4.055.86, up 49.46 points or 1.23 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,026.97, down 3.13 points, or 0.08 percent.

PARIS - Stocks rose, bolstered by record gains on Wall Street, but shares closed off their highs as late weakness in the bond market and a huge sale of Alcatel Alsthom shares weighed on the bourse, brokers said. The CAC-40 index closed at 2.950.56, up 20.75 points, or 0.71 percent.

ZURICH - Shares failed to maintain an early upward drive, snapping a four-day bull run to end lower as bourse heavyweights such as Novartis, UBS and Nestle turned negative on early Wall Street losses. The Swiss market index closed at 5,977.1, down 35.5 points, or 0.59 percent.

MILAN - The bourse set a record close but ended off the new peak set earlier in the day as a late burst of selling sent shares sharply lower. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,895, up 121 points or 0.88 percent.
AMSTERDAM - Shares closed almost two percent higher and near the day's peak as a firmer dollar boosted market sentiment. The AEX index closed at 935.37, up 17.33 points or 1.89 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks closed moderately lower as sentiment was hurt by doubts over Japan's economic recovery and concerns over the financial health of the nation's firms, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,697.17, down 156.72 points, or 0.79 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed lower after slipping into negative territory in the last half-hour of trade, chiefly on profit-taking in utilities, but brokers said the market would find support near current levels. The Hang Seng index closed at 14,703.73, down 88.44 points or 0.60 percent.

SYDNEY - Shares closed on a strong tone as gold stocks moved higher for the first time in four days and yield-sensitive stocks rose on hopes of another interest-rate cut. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,696.1, up 16.9 points or 0.63 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares renewed their downward move as sentiment took a triple knock from the ongoing bullion price fall, a shaky rand and a poorly performing bond market, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7,299.2, down 11.1 points or 0.15 percent. The All Gold index closed at 905.3, down 18.4 points or 0.08 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,759.3, down 7.0 points or 1.99 percent.
